The TB NanoString data

In this assignment you will apply unsupervised learning to the TB NanoString data: blood expression of 107 TB-related genes in 179 people with active tuberculosis (TB) or latent TB infection (LTBI) (Kaipilyawar et al., Clin Infect Dis, 2022). The first column, TB_Status, is the TB status; the remaining columns are gene expression values. You will then build a Shiny app that does dimension reduction and k-means clustering on these data.

library(tidyverse)
TBnanostring <- readRDS("TBnanostring.rds")
dim(TBnanostring)
## [1] 179 108
table(TBnanostring$TB_Status)
## 
##   TB LTBI 
##   79  100

You will need the umap (or uwot), NMF, cluster, mclust, and shiny packages.

Question 1. Principal Component Analysis (20 pts)

Task 1.1: Fit PCA and plot the variance explained (5 pts)

Run PCA on the gene expression columns (prcomp). Make a scree plot of the proportion of variance explained by each PC, and report the variance explained by PC1, PC2, and the first 10 PCs together.

gene_data <- TBnanostring %>% select(-TB_Status)

pca <- prcomp(gene_data)

pca_variance <- pca$sdev^2 / sum(pca$sdev^2)

pca_variance[1:2] * 100
## [1] 46.826175  7.289054
sum(pca_variance[1:10]) * 100
## [1] 76.23148
scree_data <- data.frame(
  PC = 1:length(pca_variance),
  Variance = pca_variance
)

ggplot(scree_data, aes(x = PC, y = Variance)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    title = "PCA Scree Plot",
    x = "Principal Component",
    y = "Proportion of Variance Explained"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

Task 1.2: PCA plot (5 pts)

Make a ggplot2 scatterplot of PC1 vs. PC2 with points colored by TB_Status. Do TB and LTBI separate? Try one other pair of PCs (e.g., PC1 vs. PC3): does it separate the groups better?

pca_scores <- as.data.frame(pca$x)

pca_scores$TB_Status <- TBnanostring$TB_Status

ggplot(pca_scores, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = TB_Status)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "PCA: PC1 vs PC2",
    x = "PC1",
    y = "PC2"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggplot(pca_scores, aes(x = PC1, y = PC3, color = TB_Status)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "PCA: PC1 vs PC3",
    x = "PC1",
    y = "PC3"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

Task 1.3: Loadings (5 pts)

Which 10 genes have the largest absolute loadings on PC1? Is PC1 related to TB status? (Hint: compare PC1 scores between the two groups with a boxplot or a t-test.)

pc1_loadings <- pca$rotation[, 1]

top10_genes <- sort(abs(pc1_loadings), decreasing = TRUE)[1:10]

top10_genes
##       TBP     LUC7L     CIRBP      MDN1    ZNF202     DARS2  CXorf40B     BATF2 
## 0.1334118 0.1328856 0.1316027 0.1304627 0.1293262 0.1289530 0.1283000 0.1275347 
##    ATP1A1     EXOC2 
## 0.1271395 0.1266948
ggplot(pca_scores, aes(x = TB_Status, y = PC1, fill = TB_Status)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "PC1 Scores by TB Status",
    x = "TB Status",
    y = "PC1 Score"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

t.test(PC1 ~ TB_Status, data = pca_scores)
## 
##  Welch Two Sample t-test
## 
## data:  PC1 by TB_Status
## t = -14.834, df = 118.56, p-value < 2.2e-16
## alternative hypothesis: true difference in means between group TB and group LTBI is not equal to 0
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  -12.301810  -9.404368
## sample estimates:
##   mean in group TB mean in group LTBI 
##          -6.063178           4.789911

Task 1.4: To scale or not to scale (5 pts)

Repeat the PCA with scale. = TRUE. How do the variance explained and the PC1 vs. PC2 plot change? Which version would you use for these data, and why?

pca_scaled <- prcomp(gene_data, scale. = TRUE)

scaled_variance <- pca_scaled$sdev^2 / sum(pca_scaled$sdev^2)

scaled_variance[1:2] * 100
## [1] 46.826175  7.289054
sum(scaled_variance[1:10]) * 100
## [1] 76.23148
scaled_scores <- as.data.frame(pca_scaled$x)

scaled_scores$TB_Status <- TBnanostring$TB_Status

ggplot(scaled_scores, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = TB_Status)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Scaled PCA: PC1 vs PC2",
    x = "PC1",
    y = "PC2"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

Scaling did not change the PCA results because all gene expression variables already had a standard deviation of 1. Therefore, the variance explained and PC1 vs. PC2 plots were identical for both analyses. I would use either version since scaling does not affect these data. ### Question 2. UMAP (15 pts)

Task 2.1: UMAP plot (5 pts)

Apply UMAP to the gene expression data (set a seed!) and plot the two UMAP dimensions colored by TB_Status.

library(umap)
set.seed(123)

umap_result <- umap(gene_data)

umap_scores <- as.data.frame(umap_result$layout)

colnames(umap_scores) <- c("UMAP1", "UMAP2")

umap_scores$TB_Status <- TBnanostring$TB_Status

ggplot(umap_scores, aes(x = UMAP1, y = UMAP2, color = TB_Status)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "UMAP of TB and LTBI Samples",
    x = "UMAP 1",
    y = "UMAP 2"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

UMAP showed partial separation between TB and LTBI samples. Most TB samples clustered toward the lower-right, while most LTBI samples were located toward the upper-left. However, some overlap was observed between the two groups. #### Task 2.2: Tuning parameters (5 pts)

Rerun UMAP with n_neighbors = 5, 15, and 50 (and, optionally, two different seeds). Show the plots side by side. How much do the pictures change?

config_5 <- umap.defaults
config_5$n_neighbors <- 5

config_15 <- umap.defaults
config_15$n_neighbors <- 15

config_50 <- umap.defaults
config_50$n_neighbors <- 50

set.seed(123)
umap_5 <- umap(gene_data, config = config_5)

set.seed(123)
umap_15 <- umap(gene_data, config = config_15)

set.seed(123)
umap_50 <- umap(gene_data, config = config_50)

plot_5 <- as.data.frame(umap_5$layout)
plot_15 <- as.data.frame(umap_15$layout)
plot_50 <- as.data.frame(umap_50$layout)

plot_5$TB_Status <- TBnanostring$TB_Status
plot_15$TB_Status <- TBnanostring$TB_Status
plot_50$TB_Status <- TBnanostring$TB_Status

plot_5$Neighbors <- "5"
plot_15$Neighbors <- "15"
plot_50$Neighbors <- "50"

umap_combined <- bind_rows(plot_5, plot_15, plot_50)

colnames(umap_combined)[1:2] <- c("UMAP1", "UMAP2")

ggplot(umap_combined, aes(x = UMAP1, y = UMAP2, color = TB_Status)) +
  geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  facet_wrap(~Neighbors) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "UMAP with Different n_neighbors Values")

Task 2.3: PCA vs. UMAP (5 pts)

Compare your PCA and UMAP plots. Which separates TB from LTBI more clearly? What can and can’t you conclude from distances between points or clusters in a UMAP plot? UMAP showed clearer separation between TB and LTBI than PCA, with some overlap between groups. UMAP preserves local similarities between samples, but distances between separate clusters should not be interpreted as exact measures of biological differences.

Question 3. Non-negative Matrix Factorization (15 pts)

Task 3.1: Prepare the data (3 pts)

NMF requires non-negative data, but these expression values are centered (some are negative). Shift each gene so its minimum is 0 (subtract each column’s minimum). Confirm that the shifted matrix has no negative values.

nmf_data <- as.matrix(gene_data)

nmf_data <- sweep(nmf_data, 2, apply(nmf_data, 2, min), "-")

min(nmf_data)
## [1] 0

Task 3.2: Fit NMF (7 pts)

Fit NMF with rank \(K = 2\) (use nrun of at least 10 and set a seed). Plot the two columns of the basis matrix \(\mathbf{W}\) (basis()) against each other, colored by TB_Status.

library(NMF)
## Loading required package: registry
## Loading required package: rngtools
## Loading required package: cluster

##   To enable shared memory capabilities, try: install.extras('
## NMF
## ')
## 
## Attaching package: 'NMF'

## 
##     fit
set.seed(123)

nmf_result <- nmf(nmf_data, rank = 2, nrun = 10)

nmf_W <- basis(nmf_result)

nmf_plot <- as.data.frame(nmf_W)

nmf_plot$TB_Status <- TBnanostring$TB_Status

ggplot(nmf_plot, aes(x = nmf_plot[,1], y = nmf_plot[,2], color = TB_Status)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "NMF Components",
    x = "Component 1",
    y = "Component 2"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

Task 3.3: Interpret the components (5 pts)

Using the coefficient matrix \(\mathbf{H}\) (coef()), list the 10 genes that load most heavily on each component. Does either component line up with TB status? How does the NMF picture compare with PCA?

nmf_H <- coef(nmf_result)

top10_comp1 <- sort(nmf_H[1, ], decreasing = TRUE)[1:10]
top10_comp2 <- sort(nmf_H[2, ], decreasing = TRUE)[1:10]

top10_comp1
##     DARS2    ATP1A1      UCP2     CIRBP      SND1      GUSB    MAP7D3  KIAA0090 
## 0.8128110 0.8049304 0.7983555 0.7896130 0.7866619 0.7826907 0.7825514 0.7727416 
##  KIAA0100      MDN1 
## 0.7721814 0.7620385
top10_comp2
##    IFI44L      GBP2    SECTM1    IFITM3      GBP4    FCGR1B     STAT1    FCGR1C 
## 0.6180840 0.5989209 0.5971245 0.5876701 0.5760952 0.5703976 0.5635274 0.5590832 
##  SERPING1    SCARF1 
## 0.5585991 0.5559356

Component 1 was enriched for genes such as DARS2 and ATP1A1, while Component 2 included immune-related genes such as IFI44L, GBP2, and STAT1. Component 1 was higher in LTBI, whereas Component 2 was higher in TB (both p < 2.2 × 10⁻¹⁶). Compared with PCA, NMF identifies distinct gene-expression patterns and separates TB-associated immune responses from other expression patterns. ### Question 4. K-means Clustering (10 pts)

Task 4.1: Choose k (4 pts)

Run k-means (nstart = 25) on the first 10 PCs from Question 1 for \(k = 1, \ldots, 10\). Make an elbow plot and a mean silhouette plot (cluster::silhouette). Which \(k\) would you choose?

pc_data <- pca_scores[, 1:10]

set.seed(123)

wss <- numeric(10)
silhouette_avg <- numeric(10)

for (k in 1:10) {
  km <- kmeans(pc_data, centers = k, nstart = 25)
  wss[k] <- km$tot.withinss

  if (k > 1) {
    sil <- cluster::silhouette(km$cluster, dist(pc_data))
    silhouette_avg[k] <- mean(sil[, 3])
  }
}

plot(1:10, wss, type = "b",
     xlab = "Number of clusters (k)",
     ylab = "Within-cluster sum of squares",
     main = "Elbow Plot")

plot(2:10, silhouette_avg[2:10], type = "b",
     xlab = "Number of clusters (k)",
     ylab = "Mean silhouette width",
     main = "Mean Silhouette Plot")

I would choose k = 2 because it has the highest mean silhouette score (0.389), indicating the best cluster separation among the tested values. The silhouette score decreases as k increases. #### Task 4.2: Clusters vs. TB status (6 pts)

Run k-means with \(k = 2\) on (a) all 107 genes, (b) the first 10 PCs, and (c) the 2 UMAP dimensions. For each, cross-tabulate the clusters with TB_Status and compute the adjusted Rand index (mclust::adjustedRandIndex). Which representation gives clusters closest to TB status? Does that mean it is the “best” representation? Explain.

set.seed(123)

km_genes <- kmeans(gene_data, centers = 2, nstart = 25)
km_pca <- kmeans(pca_scores[, 1:10], centers = 2, nstart = 25)
km_umap <- kmeans(umap_scores[, 1:2], centers = 2, nstart = 25)

table(km_genes$cluster, TBnanostring$TB_Status)
##    
##     TB LTBI
##   1 19   97
##   2 60    3
table(km_pca$cluster, TBnanostring$TB_Status)
##    
##     TB LTBI
##   1 60    3
##   2 19   97
table(km_umap$cluster, TBnanostring$TB_Status)
##    
##     TB LTBI
##   1 68   10
##   2 11   90
ari_genes <- mclust::adjustedRandIndex(km_genes$cluster, TBnanostring$TB_Status)
ari_pca <- mclust::adjustedRandIndex(km_pca$cluster, TBnanostring$TB_Status)
ari_umap <- mclust::adjustedRandIndex(km_umap$cluster, TBnanostring$TB_Status)

data.frame(
  Representation = c("All genes", "First 10 PCs", "UMAP"),
  Adjusted_Rand_Index = c(ari_genes, ari_pca, ari_umap)
)
##   Representation Adjusted_Rand_Index
## 1      All genes           0.5660855
## 2   First 10 PCs           0.5660855
## 3           UMAP           0.5834160

UMAP produced the highest ARI (0.583), indicating the closest agreement with TB status. However, this does not necessarily make it the best representation, since unsupervised clustering does not always reflect biological or clinically meaningful groupings. ### Question 5. A Shiny App for Dimension Reduction and K-means (40 pts)

Task 5.1: Walk through the k-means Shiny tutorial (10 pts)

Work step by step through the k-means Shiny app tutorial, lectures/week4/shiny_kmeans_app.html (Steps 00-09). Run the code to launch the app at each step. For each step, briefly document what changed: which functions were added and what they do in the app.

Step 00 – Template: Created the basic Shiny app structure using fluidPage(), sidebarLayout(), sidebarPanel(), mainPanel(), and shinyApp().

Step 01 – Title Panel: Added titlePanel() to display the app title.

Step 02 – UI Inputs: Added selectInput() to choose the X and Y variables and numericInput() to select the number of clusters.

Step 03 – UI Outputs: Added plotOutput() to create a location for displaying the plot.

Step 04 – Output Plot: Added renderPlot() to display a basic scatterplot.

Step 05 – Reactive Axes: Used input$xcol and input$ycol to make the plot axes respond to user selections.

Step 06 – K-means: Added kmeans() to cluster the selected variables and color points according to their cluster assignments.

Step 07 – Cluster Centers: Added points() to display cluster centers using cross-shaped markers.

Step 08 – Save K-means Result: Used reactive() to calculate and store the clustering result so it can be reused in the app.

Step 09 – Final App: Combined the inputs, reactive data selection, clustering, and plotting into a fully interactive Shiny application.

Task 5.2: Add dimension reduction and k-means on the TB data (25 pts)

Modify the final tutorial app so that it works on the TB NanoString data:

  1. Dimension reduction input: a menu to choose the method: PCA, UMAP, or NMF (rank 2).
  2. Clustering input: the number of clusters \(k\) (as in the tutorial).
  3. Plot: the two reduced dimensions, with points colored by k-means cluster and shaped by TB status; include the cluster centers.
  4. Table: a cross-tabulation of clusters vs. TB status, and the adjusted Rand index.

Tips: compute the dimension reductions once, outside the server function or in a reactive(), so the app doesn’t recompute UMAP or NMF every time \(k\) changes. Run k-means on the two reduced dimensions.

Include your app code below (with eval=FALSE) and save it as app.R.

library(shiny)
library(tidyverse)
library(umap)
library(NMF)
library(mclust)

file_path <- file.choose()
TBnanostring <- readRDS(file_path)
TBnanostring$TB_Status <- as.factor(TBnanostring$TB_Status)

gene_data <- TBnanostring %>%
  select(-TB_Status) %>%
  as.data.frame()

gene_data <- as.data.frame(lapply(gene_data, as.numeric))

pca_app <- prcomp(gene_data, center = TRUE, scale. = FALSE)
pca_embedding <- pca_app$x[, 1:2]

set.seed(123)
umap_app <- umap(as.matrix(gene_data), n_neighbors = 15, random_state = 123)
umap_embedding <- umap_app$layout

nmf_matrix <- as.matrix(gene_data)
nmf_matrix <- sweep(nmf_matrix, 2, apply(nmf_matrix, 2, min), "-")

set.seed(123)
nmf_app <- NMF::nmf(nmf_matrix, rank = 2, nrun = 10)
nmf_embedding <- basis(nmf_app)

ui <- fluidPage(
  titlePanel("TB NanoString: Dimension Reduction and K-means"),
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      selectInput("method", "Dimension reduction method",
                  choices = c("PCA", "UMAP", "NMF")),
      sliderInput("k", "Number of clusters (k)",
                  min = 2, max = 10, value = 2, step = 1)
    ),
    mainPanel(
      plotOutput("cluster_plot"),
      h4("Clusters vs. TB Status"),
      tableOutput("cluster_table"),
      textOutput("ari")
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  
  selected_embedding <- reactive({
    if (input$method == "PCA") {
      pca_embedding
    } else if (input$method == "UMAP") {
      umap_embedding
    } else {
      nmf_embedding
    }
  })
  
  clustering <- reactive({
    set.seed(123)
    kmeans(selected_embedding(), centers = input$k, nstart = 25)
  })
  
  plot_data <- reactive({
    coords <- as.data.frame(selected_embedding())
    colnames(coords) <- c("Dimension1", "Dimension2")
    coords$Cluster <- factor(clustering()$cluster)
    coords$TB_Status <- TBnanostring$TB_Status
    coords
  })
  
  output$cluster_plot <- renderPlot({
    centers <- as.data.frame(clustering()$centers)
    colnames(centers) <- c("Dimension1", "Dimension2")
    
    ggplot(plot_data(),
           aes(Dimension1, Dimension2,
               color = Cluster, shape = TB_Status)) +
      geom_point(size = 2.5) +
      geom_point(data = centers,
                 aes(Dimension1, Dimension2),
                 inherit.aes = FALSE,
                 shape = 4, size = 5, stroke = 1.5) +
      labs(title = paste(input$method, "with k-means clustering"),
           color = "Cluster", shape = "TB Status") +
      theme_minimal()
  })
  
  output$cluster_table <- renderTable({
    table(Cluster = clustering()$cluster,
          TB_Status = TBnanostring$TB_Status)
  }, rownames = TRUE)
  
  output$ari <- renderText({
    ari_value <- mclust::adjustedRandIndex(
      clustering()$cluster, TBnanostring$TB_Status
    )
    paste("Adjusted Rand Index:", round(ari_value, 3))
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
